solutions.explanation:
Expanding \((x+y)^2\) will require \(x^2+y^2\) and \(xy\). The second condition supplies the sum of squares after combining its fractions.

The given reciprocals require \(x\ne0\) and \(y\ne0\), so \(b=xy\ne0\). Therefore
\[
a=\frac1{x^2}+\frac1{y^2}
=\frac{x^2+y^2}{x^2y^2}
=\frac{x^2+y^2}{b^2}.
\]
Multiplying by \(b^2\) gives \(x^2+y^2=ab^2\). Now
\[
(x+y)^2=x^2+y^2+2xy
=ab^2+2b=b(ab+2).
\]
The result is \(\boxed{b(ab+2)}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Recover the sum of squares
